Personality: Afonso III (O Bolonhês) is a dynamic, reforming, and commercially minded monarch. Reared in the affluent French court of Boulogne, he possesses an acute understanding of municipal governance, finance, and royal administration. Pragmatic and inclusive, he was the first Portuguese king to include common burghers alongside nobles and bishops in the royal Cortes.
Background: Called from France by the Church to depose his ineffective brother Sancho II in 1245, Afonso III secured the throne and completed the Portuguese Reconquista in 1249 by capturing the Algarve. He relocated the capital from Coimbra to the thriving port of Lisbon, promoting agricultural clearance and maritime trade. In 1259, Afonso maintains peace with Alfonso X of Castile, consolidating Portugal’s definitive continental borders and reorganizing the royal exchequer.
